subject: Residency lockdown & certified sanitization process Q&A

Subject: Residency lockdown + certified sanitization process — quick questions

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. A couple follow-ups from our security team as we map out the Private/VPC deployment: we need firm answers on three things before we can proceed to procurement: 

1) Residency lock — once we select a US region and enable the VPC bundle, can you guarantee all customer-controlled storage (models, embeddings, and logs) will remain within that region and not be replicated to other regions for operational redundancy? If replication occurs, what controls let us opt out?

2) Certified sanitization — for end-of-contract teardown, we need a process that provides an auditable record showing all customer data was destroyed. Does Redwood offer cryptographic wipe / sanitization that produces a certificate or signed log? What about snapshots and backups created by the hypervisor or storage layer?

3) Time-to-complete & evidence — what are realistic SLAs for completing a full tenant sanitization (including snapshots, backups, and any cached KV entries) and what artifacts do you provide (signed attestation, retention logs, deletion runbook)?

We appreciate concise, operational answers we can give to cloud security and procurement. If helpful, loop in whoever owns the VPC operations.

Thanks,
Emma Li
Head of InfoSec, MedicoR Health

Subject: Re: Residency lockdown + certified sanitization process — quick questions

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Answering point-by-point below; I copied Dev (runtime/infrastructure) for technical specifics and Ben on the sales side to align contractual language. TL;DR: yes — we support region-locking for customer-controlled storage in Private deployments; we offer a multi-step sanitization that produces signed artifacts and a runbook for evidence. Details: 

1) Residency lock: 
- By default in Redwood Private (VPC), customer-controlled stores (object buckets for model artifacts, dedicated embedding stores, and inference logs when configured) are pinned to the selected cloud region and the customer VPC. 
- System-level replication for cross-region HA is not enabled unless explicitly requested in the deployment options; if a customer opts for cross-region replication that is fully managed by Redwood, we require an explicit change order.
- For workloads that enable our optional DR replication, we provide a per-resource flag at provisioning time (replicate: true/false) so you can opt out.

2) Certified sanitization (overview): 
We run a three-phased disposal flow for Private tenants: 
  a) Logical purge — application-layer deletion of tenant records and tombstoning. We log each deletion event.
  b) Snapshot & backup sweep — identify all snapshots/backups associated with the tenant (cloud block snapshots, object versioning entries, DB backups) and queue them for deletion according to cloud provider APIs. For providers that do not allow immediate snapshot purge, we mark those items "pending destruction" and track lifecycle state until provider completes removal.
  c) Cryptographic key destruction & low-level sanitization — if tenant data is protected with a customer-managed KMS key or Redwood-managed envelope keys, we include explicit key-sunset steps: deleting encryption keys (where permitted) renders ciphertext practically unrecoverable. For disk-level artifacts we use provider-approved secure deletion APIs where available.

We produce a signed "Sanitization Certificate" after the flow completes that includes: list of resources purged, timestamps, deletion ops and request IDs (cloud provider), and a signature from Redwood's Compliance Service. See attached: sanitization-checklist.pdf and vpc-data-lifecycle-diagram.png.

3) SLA & artifacts: 
- Typical completion window: 72 hours for the Logical purge + manifesting deletion operations. 
- Snapshot/backups: depends on cloud provider retention windows; if immediate purge APIs are available we complete within 7 days. If provider retention prevents immediate purge (e.g., snapshot immutability windows), we provide a documented timeline and track the resource until provider permits deletion.
- Artifacts provided: sanitized resource manifest (CSV), deletion operation logs (cloud request IDs), and a signed Sanitization Certificate (PDF). We can also export a compliance bundle (zip) containing the raw provider responses for audits.

Attachments: [attachment: sanitization-checklist.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: vpc-data-lifecycle-diagram.png (png)].

If you want, Ben can include the certificate language as a contract exhibit and we can add a provider-specific appendix for the cloud region you select.

—Kimberly Park

A) Snapshots created by the host (EBS/PD snapshots) — are those tied to a tenant identifier so they get swept automatically, or can host snapshots be orphaned by name? We need assurance that every snapshot has a deterministic mapping back to our tenant.

B) Object store replication — some of our workloads use versioned object buckets for model checkpoints. We want to confirm whether object versioning metadata (older versions) are tracked in your manifest and whether the Sanitization Certificate will list deletion of historical versions too.

Also, is there a template we can use to request a deletion (internal ticket) so we can keep our procurement records tidy?

Emma — quick technical clarifications: 

A) Host snapshots: 
- We tag all infrastructure-level snapshots created on behalf of a Private tenant with a tenant UUID and resource tag (redwood:tenant_id=<tenant-uuid>). Our discovery agents query provider APIs to enumerate snapshots by tag at sweep time. If a snapshot is orphaned (missing tag), it shows up in a manual review queue; we do not automatically include orphaned snapshots in the purge until the review is resolved, and we surface these as "orphan candidates" in the manifest so customers can approve/deny removal. 

B) Object store versioning: 
- For versioned buckets we record all object versions and deletion markers in the purge manifest. The Sanitization Certificate will include counts and checksums for removed versions when provider APIs return checksum metadata. We also include markers for non-destructively overwritten objects when immediate deletion is not permitted by provider.

C) Deletion request template: 
- Created a lightweight template for your internal ticketing: deletion-request-template.docx. It includes required fields (tenant UUID, requested date, desired retention exceptions, legal hold flags, and point of contact). We can pre-fill the tenant UUID once account provisioning completes.

Operational note: if you plan to hold long-term snapshots for regulatory reasons, we recommend documenting retention exceptions during contracting so we can exclude those resources from automatic purge flows.

—Dev Patel
